open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token” versus K-15, which defines only agent tokens
open_points.question: Where is the owner's token configured, how is it distinguished from agent tokens, and how is it rotated or revoked?
options: A separately configured owner bearer token
Host or reverse-proxy authentication mapped to the owner
The owner uses an author-capable agent token with an additional assertion
open_points.default_guess: Use a separately configured owner token and reload it on configuration change.

open_points.subject: platform manifest
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest”
open_points.question: Who supplies and controls the manifest, how the kernel obtains it, and whether its contents are trusted or authenticated are not stated.
options: A trusted local installation file
A signed manifest fetched from the platform
An untrusted source whose records require independent verification
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as trusted installation configuration loaded from a local file.

open_points.subject: outside-material submission
open_points.text: “Their material stays at a microservice's own intake until the owner or an agent submits it” versus “a caller never hands the kernel a file”
open_points.question: What concrete kernel action submits outside material, what reference or value it accepts, and what it returns or refuses are not stated.
options: Running a flow with the service intake-record identifier
A distinct submit-intake-record action
An operation node discovers pending intake records without a caller-supplied reference
open_points.default_guess: Pass an intake-record identifier as a value when running a flow.

open_points.subject: withheld secret echoes
open_points.text: “A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld”
open_points.question: What does the caller, flow, node, run and trace observe when a service response is withheld because it contains a secret?
options: Fail the node with a secret-detected reason
Return only a digest and class
Suppress the field while allowing the remaining response
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node, retain only a digest, and record a secret-detected failure without the value.

open_points.subject: owner access to secret-bearing values
open_points.text: “The owner receives every value” versus “A service's own answer that echoes [a secret] verbatim is withheld”
open_points.question: Does the secret-withholding rule override the promise that the owner receives every value?
options: Withhold secrets from every actor, including the owner
Return the value to the owner but withhold it from agents
Reject the entire service response before it becomes a value
open_points.default_guess: Withhold the secret-bearing response from every actor, including the owner.

open_points.subject: slot and contract-version identity
open_points.text: “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot” and “A contract is an immutable versioned declaration”
open_points.question: What identifies a slot and a contract version, and how does an author request a new version of an existing slot rather than idempotently returning an equal version?
options: Slot name plus a content-digest contract version
Slot name plus a kernel-assigned monotonically increasing version
A separate slot identifier plus an explicit parent contract version
open_points.default_guess: Use the slot name and a canonical content digest, with equal content returning the existing version.

open_points.subject: implementation submission and admission
open_points.text: “try an implementation” and “admit and activate — kernel, when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: Does authoring an implementation automatically run the whole corpus and admit it, does the try action trigger admission, or are trial and admission separate requests?
options: Authoring automatically tries the whole corpus and admits or refuses
Try triggers whole-corpus admission and activation
Try produces evidence, followed by a separate admission request
open_points.default_guess: Authoring stores the implementation, while try runs the corpus and automatically admits and activates on success.

open_points.subject: invalid implementation refusal
open_points.text: “invalid contract or code refused with the reason”
open_points.question: Which code defects cause authoring itself to refuse, rather than being stored and later failing a trial or sandbox execution?
options: Only malformed Python or an invalid package shape
Any statically detected forbidden capability or import
No code-level refusal at authoring; all code failures occur during trials
open_points.default_guess: Refuse malformed Python and forbidden imports statically; leave runtime violations to trials.

open_points.subject: trial-case oracle
open_points.text: “add a trial case” and “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus … every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: What data constitutes a trial case, especially what expected output or success predicate is supplied when the captured execution failed and may have produced no valid output?
options: Inputs plus an explicitly authored expected output
Inputs plus a schema-valid-success predicate only
Inputs plus an owner-approved expected output added during capture
open_points.default_guess: Require inputs and an explicit expected output; capturing a failure must also supply or select that expected output.

open_points.subject: active trial corpus
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus” versus “Cases are … not withdrawn”
open_points.question: What makes a case active or inactive if cases cannot be withdrawn and no action changes their activity?
options: Every case belonging to the contract version is always active
Cases have activation state changed by an unlisted action
Only the latest case for equal inputs is active
open_points.default_guess: Treat every case of the contract version as permanently active.

open_points.subject: function file output
open_points.text: “no filesystem beyond its input” versus “A file port accepts exactly one media type; a function that can produce two kinds of file has two ports”
open_points.question: How can a function produce a file output if its sandbox has filesystem access only to its input?
options: A writable output-only directory is also mounted
File output is emitted through a bounded byte stream rather than the filesystem
Functions may consume files but may not actually produce them
open_points.default_guess: Provide distinct read-only input and writable output directories, with only declared output files collected.

open_points.subject: value schemas
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema. An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
open_points.question: What schema language and canonical equality rule determine whether two schemas are the same?
options: Canonical JSON Schema equality
Named immutable schema identifiers
A kernel-specific closed type algebra
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed kernel type algebra with canonical serialization and digest equality.

open_points.subject: flow interface
open_points.text: “A flow is an immutable, acyclic graph” and “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values”
open_points.question: How are a flow's input and output ports declared, typed and connected to nodes, and can a flow contain literal values?
options: Explicit typed flow input and output ports represented as graph endpoints
Inputs inferred from unconnected node ports and outputs inferred from terminal ports
A single structured input and output value for every flow
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit typed flow input and output endpoints and no undeclared literals.

open_points.subject: map and guard semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection, and a guard on a declared closed value”
open_points.question: The collection type, result ordering, per-item failure behavior, guard comparison, false-branch behavior and resulting output are not stated.
options: Ordered map with fail-fast behavior and a guard that skips its guarded node
Ordered map with per-item results and a guard with explicit true and false branches
Unordered map with aggregate failure and a guard that produces an optional value
open_points.default_guess: Use ordered mapping, fail the mapped node if any item fails, and have a false guard mark the guarded branch skipped with no output.

open_points.subject: operation authority metadata
open_points.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`” and “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: Who assigns an operation's effect class, where that class and the idempotency-key declaration are stored, and what prevents an agent from understating the authority required?
options: Both are trusted fields of the platform manifest operation record
The agent proposes them and the owner accepts them in the binding
The manifest supplies capabilities while the binding assigns the effect class
open_points.default_guess: Make both trusted fields of the manifest operation record and pin them through the binding.

open_points.subject: idempotency-key semantics
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: The key's generation, scope, placement, persistence and reuse across resume or unknown-outcome resolution are not stated.
options: One key per run and operation-node execution, reused for every send attempt
One key per approval
A key derived deterministically from the fully built request
open_points.default_guess: Generate one opaque key per run/node execution, persist it before sending, and reuse it for every attempt of that execution.

open_points.subject: run inputs
open_points.text: “run a flow — owner, agent — a run of the flow's active version, with outputs”
open_points.question: What input values the caller supplies, how they are matched to flow inputs, and what happens on missing, extra or schema-invalid values are not stated.
options: A named map of values validated against explicit flow input ports
A positional list inferred from source nodes
No direct inputs; all flows must obtain values from service operations
open_points.default_guess: Accept a named map validated against explicit flow input ports and refuse the start on missing, extra or invalid values.

open_points.subject: classification of caller-supplied and zero-input values
open_points.text: “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`” and “a function's output takes the highest class its execution received”
open_points.question: Who assigns the class of flow inputs, trial fixtures and literals, and what class a zero-input function's output receives are not stated.
options: Their declarations fix the class
The submitting actor labels each value subject to validation
All such values default to `open`
open_points.default_guess: Declare the maximum or fixed class on every flow input and fixture, and classify a zero-input function's output as `open`.

open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the highest class each input accepts” and “an input accepting less”
open_points.question: What exact ordering and comparison rule applies to the three disclosure classes?
options: `open` < `business_confidential` < `personal_data`
`business_confidential` and `personal_data` are incomparable above `open`
Inputs declare an explicit allowed set rather than an ordering
open_points.default_guess: Use the total order `open` < `business_confidential` < `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: standing-approval eligibility
open_points.text: “grant a standing approval for a node” with only “a `destructive` node … cannot be granted”
open_points.question: Can grants be created for `read` and `draft-write` nodes that do not normally ask, or only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes?
options: Only `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes
Every non-destructive operation node
Every node, although grants on non-stopping nodes have no effect
open_points.default_guess: Permit grants only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` operation nodes.

open_points.subject: approval result when sending fails
open_points.text: “approve or refuse an effect … the effect runs on the exact input shown” versus “An approval whose effect was never sent (the service was unreachable) stays valid on resume”
open_points.question: What observable result does the approve action return when the approved request cannot be sent, receives an invalid response, or has an unknown outcome?
options: Return the updated pending run and retained approval
Treat approval as successful independently of the later send result
Make approval and sending separate actions
open_points.default_guess: Return the updated run; it becomes pending for unreachable or unknown outcomes while retaining the approval where no send occurred.

open_points.subject: resolved-applied operation output
open_points.text: “the effect is recorded applied, or not applied; the run continues”
open_points.question: When an unknown outcome is resolved as applied but no validated response was received, what output value feeds dependent nodes?
options: Applied effects must have no output ports used downstream
The owner supplies or selects the missing output during resolution
Dependent nodes are skipped and the run succeeds with no value
The run records the effect as applied but fails if downstream output is required
open_points.default_guess: Allow resolution as applied, but fail any dependent path that requires an unavailable output.

open_points.subject: cancellation of in-flight work
open_points.text: “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent”
open_points.question: What happens to function executions and HTTP requests already in progress when cancellation is requested, and can their effects or trace results arrive after the run is marked cancelled?
options: Wait for in-flight work to settle, then mark cancelled
Mark cancelled immediately and ignore late results, acknowledging that an already-sent effect may complete
Attempt cooperative cancellation and leave the run pending if an effect's outcome becomes unknown
open_points.default_guess: Stop scheduling immediately, attempt cancellation, record any already-sent effect honestly, and use outcome-unknown when its result cannot be determined.

open_points.subject: partial branch failure
open_points.text: “a failed node stops its dependants” and “A failed node stops only its dependants”
open_points.question: Do independent branches continue, what outputs are returned from successful branches, and when does the overall run enter `failed`?
options: Independent branches finish and partial outputs remain inspectable; the run then ends failed
The first node failure ends the whole run immediately
Independent branches finish but all flow outputs are suppressed on overall failure
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches, retain their trace outputs, and end the run failed after no runnable work remains.

open_points.subject: simultaneous waiting reasons
open_points.text: “A run rests `awaiting_approval`, or `pending` when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown” versus “resume … whatever else the run waits for”
open_points.question: How is a run represented when different nodes simultaneously await approval, an unreachable service and an unknown outcome, and which top-level status takes precedence?
options: One top-level status with an explicit precedence rule plus per-node wait reasons
A set of run statuses with no single status
A generic waiting run status with all reasons listed
open_points.default_guess: Use per-node wait reasons and a single top-level status with `pending/outcome_unknown` above `pending/unreachable` above `awaiting_approval`.

open_points.subject: trace reading failure
open_points.text: “read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —” despite “Each action names its observable output and its failure”
open_points.question: What happens when the requested run or trace is unknown, malformed, inaccessible, or refers to released files?
options: Refuse unknown references and return retained records without released payloads
Return an empty result for unknown references
Trace reads cannot name a trace and only stream all records
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unknown references and return metadata or digests for payloads whose files were released.

open_points.subject: business facts in retained values
open_points.text: “It stores no business fact” versus “bounded values that edges carry” and “Values … are kept for as long as the kernel keeps its traces; this kernel expires nothing”
open_points.question: Are business values such as invoice identifiers, amounts and analysis results retained in the kernel indefinitely as edge or trace values, or must such values be reduced to digests?
options: Retain bounded business values as execution evidence; ‘no business fact’ means no authoritative domain records
Retain only digests for business values
Retain values only while the run is active
open_points.default_guess: Retain bounded values as non-authoritative execution evidence and define ‘no business fact’ to mean no authoritative business record.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel” versus the primary actions for add trial case, admit, capture, release, rollback, propose binding, compose and prove, and agent activation of read-only flows
open_points.question: Which MCP operations expose every listed primary action, and may an agent invoke activation for a read-only flow as K-08 requires?
options: Add every primary action as its own MCP operation
Define named subcommands under the broad `author`, `try` and `activate` operations
Remove the unmatched primary actions from the product surface
open_points.default_guess: Expose each materially different primary action explicitly and allow agent activation requests only for proven read-only versions.

open_points.subject: repair context recency
open_points.text: “that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”
open_points.question: What makes traces or evidence recent, how many are returned, and whether the complete active trial corpus is always included are not stated.
options: A fixed count per category
A fixed time window
Caller pagination with the whole active corpus always available
open_points.default_guess: Return the whole active corpus and a bounded newest-first page of traces with pagination.

open_points.subject: repository continuity
open_points.text: “the platform manifest and the repositories alone”
open_points.question: Which repositories are required, what records or code each contains, how an agent accesses them, and what observable check proves a second agent can continue are not stated.
options: The kernel source repository plus separate function and service repositories
One installation repository containing all non-kernel artifacts
Repositories are documentation only and all operative state is inspectable from the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Require named installation, kernel and service repositories, and test continuity by giving a fresh agent only those repositories, the manifest and kernel inspection access.

open_points.subject: photo-upload acceptance case
open_points.text: “takes an original invoice photo into custody … it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`”
open_points.question: Which operation owns custody, which effect class is expected, why the run becomes pending, what evidence must be observed, and whether the case must subsequently resolve or finish are not stated.
options: An unknown-outcome send followed by owner resolution
An unreachable service followed by resume
Either pending reason is sufficient and no terminal completion is required
open_points.default_guess: Require an external-effect custody operation, capture an unknown outcome after send, show the exact approved request and stable idempotency key, resolve it as applied, and finish successfully.

open_points.subject: third-party-analysis acceptance case
open_points.text: “Within one conversation … returns an analysis, releasing nothing”
open_points.question: What input dataset, expected analysis or correctness criterion, conversation boundary, recipient, and meaning of ‘releasing nothing’ define a pass?
options: A fixed fixture with an exact expected analysis and no effectful operation nodes
A schema-valid analysis judged by the owner with no external writes
Any returned value from a read-only proven flow
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed service fixture and exact expected result, return it to the requesting agent subject to disclosure rules, and require that no non-read operation or external data release occurs.

open_points.subject: acceptance service environment
open_points.text: “both cases pass against the real service instances” versus “Effectful flows are rehearsed on an installation of disposable rigs”
open_points.question: Does the effectful photo case run against production-like real instances, disposable real service rigs, or both?
options: Disposable instances running the real service implementations
Production instances for acceptance and rigs only for rehearsal
Both environments with separate pass criteria
open_points.default_guess: Run acceptance against disposable instances of the real service implementations.

open_points.subject: closed-question claim
open_points.text: “Open questions — None” and “closed means the question no longer comes back”
open_points.question: Are the unresolved action, actor, state and acceptance choices above intended to be fixed by this State 0, or explicitly delegated to named later states?
options: Resolve them in State 0
List each as intentionally delegated with its owning later state
Remove the promises that depend on them
open_points.default_guess: Resolve product-visible behavior and trust boundaries in State 0, while explicitly assigning only implementation mechanics to later states.
